report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of _ollama_native.py: two functions (_native_calls, native_chat) with docstring claims about Ollama API adaptation, HTTP error handling, and format constraints.
risks: _native_calls | medium | Assumes tool_calls structure; malformed input may cause silent fallback to empty arguments. | Add explicit validation or error logging for unexpected tool_calls shapes.

native_chat | medium | Raises ProviderHTTPError on HTTP/URL/Timeout errors; matches claimed behavior but error messages may leak internal details. | Ensure error messages are safe for user-facing output.

native_chat | low | Docstring claims 'format:"json" sent only when force_json' but code sends 'format' key with dict or string 'json'; if force_json is a dict, format is a schema dict, not 'json'. Claim is kept but note nuance.
native_chat | low | num_ctx default uses num_ctx_value() which is not defined in this chunk; behavior depends on external definition. | Ensure num_ctx_value is defined and imported.

handoff.purpose: Defines _native_calls helper and native_chat function for Ollama /api/chat endpoint.

symbols.name: _native_calls
symbols.note: Transforms Ollama's tool_calls format to OpenAI-compatible shape; handles string arguments by JSON parsing.

symbols.name: native_chat
symbols.note: Sends POST to /api/chat with options; returns adapted message dict; raises ProviderHTTPError on failures.

claims.text: POST ``messages`` to Ollama's native ``/api/chat`` and return the assistant message adapted to the OpenAI shape (see :func:`_adapt_message`).
claims.why: Code constructs URL with '/api/chat', sends POST with messages, and returns _adapt_message(message).

claims.text: ``options.num_ctx`` (defaulting to :func:`num_ctx_value`) is the whole point of this path -- it is the only way to lift the ~2050-token ``/v1`` cap.
claims.why: Code sets options.num_ctx using num_ctx_value() as default, but claim about /v1 cap and comparison is outside this chunk.

claims.text: ``num_predict`` is optional and omitted by default, preserving every existing caller; bounded rewrite callers use it to prevent a malformed JSON generation from consuming the entire remaining context window.
claims.why: Code only adds num_predict to body if it is not None, and clamps to max(1, int(num_predict)).

claims.text: ``think`` is likewise opt-in. Structured edit callers disable hidden reasoning so a bounded generation cannot spend its entire token allowance before emitting the required JSON value.
claims.why: Code only adds 'think' key if think is not None, converting to bool.

claims.text: ``format:"json"`` is sent only when ``force_json``; ``keep_alive`` and ``tools`` only when provided.
claims.why: Code conditionally adds format (if force_json truthy), keep_alive (if not None), and tools (if truthy).

claims.text: Raises :class:`ProviderHTTPError` on any HTTP error or an unreachable host, mirroring ``_openai_compat._post``.
claims.why: Code raises ProviderHTTPError on HTTPError, URLError, and TimeoutError with descriptive messages.

claims.text: A dict is a JSON *schema*, and that distinction is load-bearing. ``format:"json"`` only promises valid JSON of any shape; a schema constrains the SHAPE at the sampler, masking invalid tokens instead of validating after the fact.
claims.why: Claim about Ollama's behavior with format vs schema is not verifiable from this code alone; depends on Ollama server.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-29 on the bench, 3 trials x 2 tasks per model, native `tools` array vs schema-constrained decoding: ...
claims.why: Benchmark results are external performance claims; not verifiable from code.

claims.text: The three that scored zero were not failing to *decide* -- they were failing to EMIT the decision in the structured form, narrating it in prose instead, which the harness reads as a successful turn that did nothing. Constraining the shape removes the failure entirely, on the 4.5GB model as well as the 22GB one.
claims.why: Analysis of model behavior is external claim; not verifiable from code.

observations.what: Function _native_calls assumes tool_calls is a list of dicts; if not, it falls back to empty arguments silently.
native_chat uses num_ctx_value() which is not defined in this chunk; its behavior depends on external definition.
observations.where: native_chat, line body['options']['num_ctx'] = num_ctx or num_ctx_value()

observations.what: Error messages in ProviderHTTPError include URL and detail, which may leak internal network paths or sensitive info.

Docstring claims 'format:"json" sent only when force_json' but code sends format as dict if force_json is a dict, else string 'json'. The claim is accurate for the string case, but note that a dict schema is not 'json'.
observations.where: native_chat, line body['format'] = force_json if isinstance(force_json, dict) else 'json'
